subject: Copywriting
title: Transparency as Persuasion
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Transparency as Persuasion.

hook.text: Patagonia ran an ad saying 'Don't Buy This Jacket.' Sales increased 30%. Honesty was more persuasive than promotion.

buildup.text: When a brand admits downsides, credibility soars. Avis's 'We try harder' acknowledged second place and profited.

discovery.text: Psychologists call it the 'blemish effect.' One small flaw mentioned honestly makes all other claims more believable.

twist.text: Transparency works only when authentic. Performative honesty—fake flaws chosen for marketing—gets exposed fast.

climax.text: Buffer publishes salaries publicly. Everlane shows factory costs. Radical transparency is now a brand strategy.

punchline.text: Admit a flaw, gain trust. Honesty outsells perfection.

quiz.question: What is the 'blemish effect'?
options: A small admitted flaw makes other claims more believable
